nodes.body:

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS 26.2 Tahoe

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A never worked

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The Claude in Chrome extension (ID: fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn) should load and function in an Electron app, allowing users to interact with Claude AI within the browser window.


### Actual Behavior

The extension loads but immediately throws multiple errors related to missing Chrome APIs. The extension's service worker fails to register and core functionality doesn't work.


### Testcase Gist URL

N/A

### Additional Information

**Console Output:**
```
(node:27824) ExtensionLoadWarning: Warnings loading extension at /Users/david/Desktop/claude-browser/claude-extension/1.0.52_0:
  Permission 'sidePanel' is unknown.
  Permission 'debugger' is unknown.
  Permission 'tabGroups' is unknown.
  Permission 'notifications' is unknown.
  Permission 'webNavigation' is unknown.
  Permission 'downloads' is unknown.

[27824:0217/183751.561263:ERROR:extensions/browser/extensions_browser_client.cc:81] Extension Error:
  OTR:     false
  Level:   2
  Source:  chrome-extension://fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn/assets/mcpPermissions-C5l1E_pE.js
  Message: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'onEvent')
  ID:      fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn
  Type:    RuntimeError

[27824:0217/183751.561501:ERROR:extensions/browser/extensions_browser_client.cc:81] Extension Error:
  Level:   1
  Source:  manifest.json
  Message: Service worker registration failed. Status code: 15
  Type:    ManifestError
```

**Extension Details:**
- Extension: Claude in Chrome (Anthropic)
- Version: 1.0.52
- Chrome Web Store ID: fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn

**Missing APIs:**
The extension requires several Chrome-specific APIs that appear to be unsupported or partially implemented in Electron:
- `chrome.sidePanel` - for sidebar UI
- `chrome.debugger` - for browser control
- `chrome.tabGroups` - for tab management
- `chrome.webNavigation` - for navigation events
- `chrome.downloads` - for file downloads

This follows up on issue #49584 where a moderator suggested trying the extension and reporting specific errors if it doesn't work.

nodes.title: ProcessSingleton IPC corrupts additional_data when argv contains chars above U+00FF combined with spaces

nodes.diff:
## Description

On Linux, when an Electron app is launched with command-line arguments containing **both** a space and a multi-byte UTF-8 character (emoji, CJK, etc.), the GPU subprocess fails to initialize and the process hangs indefinitely. This does not occur on Windows.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Works (no spaces in argument with emoji)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello🎉world"

# Hangs indefinitely (space + emoji in same argument)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello 🎉 world"

# Works (spaces but no emoji)
/path/to/electron-app --no-sandbox some-command content="hello world"
```

The GPU process logs:
```
ERROR:components/viz/service/main/viz_main_impl.cc:189] Exiting GPU process due to errors during initialization
```

Confirmed via `strace -f`: child/zygote processes hang while reading `/proc/self/cmdline`.

## Environment

- **OS**: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8.0, Docker container with no GPU hardware)
- **Electron**: 33+ (via Obsidian 1.12.1, but reproducible with any Electron app on Linux)
- **GPU**: None (software rendering) — but the bug is in command-line parsing, not GPU initialization itself

## Root Cause Analysis

The bug is in `base/command_line.cc` in `AppendSwitchesAndArguments` and `SetProgram`:

```cpp
// Windows — Unicode-aware ✅
arg = CommandLine::StringType(TrimWhitespace(arg, TRIM_ALL));

// Linux/POSIX — ASCII-only, byte-by-byte ❌
TrimWhitespaceASCII(arg, TRIM_ALL, &arg);
```

`TrimWhitespaceASCII` operates byte-by-byte on what it assumes is an ASCII string. When arguments contain multi-byte UTF-8 characters (3+ bytes, e.g., emoji `0xF0 0x9F 0x8E 0x89`), it doesn't understand character boundaries.

The chain of events:

1. CLI launches with emoji + spaces in argv
2. Zygote forks a GPU child process
3. Child calls `CommandLine::InitFromArgv()` → `AppendSwitchesAndArguments` runs `TrimWhitespaceASCII` on each argument byte-by-byte
4. `SetProcessTitleFromCommandLine` flattens all args into a single space-separated string and writes it over the original argv memory via `setproctitle`
5. `/proc/self/cmdline` now contains corrupted data
6. GPU subprocess reads corrupted command line → switches like `--type=gpu-process` are malformed → GPU initialization fails → process hangs

### Why each condition is required:

- **Without spaces**: `TrimWhitespaceASCII` has nothing to trim, multi-byte bytes (all > 0x7F) pass through unmodified
- **Without multi-byte UTF-8**: Pure ASCII, byte-level operations work correctly
- **With both**: Byte-level trimming near space + multi-byte boundaries corrupts string length calculations, which cascades through `setproctitle` into corrupted `/proc/self/cmdline`

### Why Windows is unaffected:

- Uses `TrimWhitespace` (Unicode-aware) instead of `TrimWhitespaceASCII`
- Does not use the zygote/fork model
- Does not have `setproctitle` or `/proc/self/cmdline`

## Suggested Fix

Use `TrimWhitespace` (or a UTF-8-aware equivalent) instead of `TrimWhitespaceASCII` on POSIX in `base/command_line.cc`. The ASCII-only assumption is incorrect on modern Linux systems where argv can contain arbitrary UTF-8.

## Real-World Impact

This affects any Electron-based CLI tool on Linux that accepts user content as arguments (e.g., note-taking apps, automation tools). Users cannot pass emoji or CJK characters with spaces in command-line arguments without the process hanging.

## Related Reports

- [Obsidian Forum: CLI command hangs with multibyte characters](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/cli-command-hangs-when-creating-notes-with-multibyte-characters-cjk-unicode/111035)
- [Chromium discussion: GPU process fails with multibyte username](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-discuss/c/4OgTFSPxP68)

nodes.title: `webUtils.getNativeVideoFrameHandle(frame)` for Zero-Copy VideoFame GPU Handoff
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, high-performance video applications in Electron (e.g., those using node-av, ffmpeg, or custom C++ encoding/AI pipelines) lack a supported way to access the underlying GPU handle of a VideoFrame directly from Renderer process to send it to the main process quickly, without performing GPU<>CPU copy.

It is a primary bottleneck in high-performance scenarios of encoding video frames created by the renderer process.



### Proposed Solution

Proposed API Expanding the [webUtils](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-utils)) module to provide way to extract gpu memory pointer from `VideoFrame` which can instantly be sent to the main process, where it will be able to process it using native node bindings, such as https://seydx.github.io/node-av/api/lib/classes/Frame.html#fromiosurface

```ts
  const videoFrame = new VideoFrame(canvas, options); // I capture frame from <canvas />, often sub-ms performance
  // VideoFrame is already in GPU memory now
  // we can obtain GPU memory pointer
  const handle = webUtils.getNativeVideoFrameHandle(videoFrame);
  
  if (handle) {
    // Zero-copy: We have GPU pointer, we can send it to main process
    ipcRenderer.send('process-gpu-handle', handle.iosurface); // platform specific handles, same as shared texture
  }
```

Then main process can use API like 

```ts
import { Frame, HardwareFramesContext } from 'node-av/lib';

const frame = Frame.fromIOSurface(ioSurfaceBuffer, {
  hwFramesCtx,
  pts: 0n,
  timeBase: { num: 1, den: 90000 },
});
```

and start encoding it

The flow would be:
- renderer process paints frame on canvas, captures `VideoFrame` (often sub-ms even for 4k frame)
- at this point my `VideoFrame` is already in GPU memory. I just need to make it usable on main process side quickly
- using proposed API, I obtain GPU memory pointer
- I send this pointer to main process using IPC
- main process uses some native bindings, like `node-av` to instantly start processing the frame
- when done, renderer is responsible to close the video frame to release resources.

### Alternatives Considered

Moving frames from the Renderer to the Main process currently requires one of:

- CPU Readback: Using copyTo() to move pixels to an ArrayBuffer. This is extremely expensive at 4K/60fps and negates the benefits of hardware decoding.

- Private Hacks: Disabling the sandbox to use Node.js native addons that attempt to "guess" memory offsets of Chromium's internal media::VideoFrame objects. This is fragile across Electron versions and insecure.

- Using `paint` event with shared textures. It works, but even if high fpu values on browser window, waiting for paint event often takes ~8-20ms for large textures which is quite bad considering I already have `VideoFrame` created in the renderer process, so what I need is already in GPU memory, I don't need a separate one from the paint event which is equal to the one I have already

- Also, it is possible to encode directly inside the Renderer process, using hardware-accelerated `VideoEncoder`, but from my experiments it seems using native node<>ffmpeg bridge (like `node-av`) could be ~2-3x faster if there was a quick way to zero-copy pass my videoframe to the main process

- Also, it is possible to use `browserWindow.webContents.capturePage()` to get `NativeImage`, and then `getNativeHandle()` thet will return `NSImage` (macOS) memory pointer, which works with eg https://seydx.github.io/node-av/api/lib/classes/Frame.html#fromnsimage , but `.capturePage()` often takes ~10-40ms, which again makes it unusable in high-performance scenarios, especially knowing I already have the needed texture in GPU memory, but on the renderer side and I only need to pass the pointer.

I am quite confident I did really try all possible, existing solutions.

### Additional Information

Electron's internal C++ implementation would likely unwrap the blink::VideoFrame, access its media::VideoFrame, and extract the gfx::GpuMemoryBuffer.

Security: By implementing this in webUtils, Electron maintains the security model. The Renderer never sees the raw pointer, only a system-level ID that the Main process (trusted) can resolve.

Note: the new API could only support gpu-based video frames. For ones created from `ArrayBuffer`, `DataView` or typed arrays, I think the API could throw an error or return null, as in this scenario, we create VideoFrame from data we already have in CPU memory, so zero-copy scenario is quite irrelevant

nodes.body:

### Electron Version

40.2.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

If `useSharedTexture` is enabled, shared texture should be created with same directx texture flags for any `pixelFormat` in `OffscreenSharedTexture` object.

### Actual Behavior

Shared textures are created with different directx texture flags.

To be specific
* Shared texture with `pixelFormat: bgra` is created only with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` flag as stated documentation.
* Shared texture with `pixelFormat: rgbaf16` is created with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` and `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_KEYEDMUTEX` flags. So `IDXGIKeyedMutex` must be acquired and locked with key `0`. Without this, all GPU operations, such as copying and drawing, will perform as if the texture were transparent, without any error.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Shared textures should be created using same flags, or at least the differences should be clearly stated in the documentation.

nodes.title: Add documentation for `app.getApplicationNameForProtocol` performance disparity between Linux and macOS/Windows

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The `app.getApplicationNameForProtocol` API performs noticeably slower on Linux, as compared to Windows and macOS.

This problem requires the API to be called repeatedly without caching to be visible, and can result in builds on Windows and macOS performing fine during testing, whilst Linux builds are disproportionately less performant.

Yes, this only appears if a developer doesn't cache the output of this API. I believe that makes it more important, as it becomes easier to overlook during testing.

### Proposed Solution

Document this performance disparity regarding how builds for Linux can run much slower, whilst appearing fine on Windows and macOS.

### Alternatives Considered

I did consider that Linux could cache the output of the API. I don't believe that's a good idea, and this would also require a code change.

### Additional Information

I had a look at the source code. The Linux API calls a shell command, and I think macOS and Windows use system APIs. I'm not completely sure about macOS.

nodes.title: `window.open()` could be documented better
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

This is inspired by #11219, and is a potential duplicate of it (but with a wider scope). Right now [our documentation on the use of `window.open` in the renderer](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v40.2.1/docs/api/window-open.md#windowopenurl-framename-features) reads as follows:
> Electron will parse [`BrowserWindowConstructorOptions`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/structures/browser-window-options) out of this list where possible, for convenience. For full control and better ergonomics, consider using `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` to customize the BrowserWindow creation.

### Proposed Solution

The "where possible" here is a bit vague and while the push towards `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` is probably warranted, I believe the docs could be improved by more explicitly calling out [what feature strings we actually support there (which is arguably more limited than what the wording here would suggest).](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v40.2.0/lib/browser/parse-features-string.ts#L78)

### Alternatives Considered

We could also just continue to let the encouragement to use `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` do the heavy lifting for us and not bother with explaining the specific inner workings of a less-capable feature.

### Additional Information

_No response_
